title: Final two changes — then the design is settled
lead: Space flips Before/After. Both of these are the changes you asked for on 2026-08-27; nothing else moved.

items.title: The state tab is an accent now

points.what: The state was a full-width solid bar across the top of the row — the loudest thing on the screen.
points.fix: It is now a small centred tab hanging off the top edge, one type size smaller.
points.why:
What did not change: it is still a solid fill with black text. That is the part carrying the contrast, and softening it back into a translucent tint is precisely what made the label invisible on Crème and Light two rounds ago.

So I shrank it rather than quietening its colour, and re-measured at the smaller size: 6.65:1 on Crème, against the 4.5 needed for 9px text. It is smaller and still readable, which is the only version of "less prominent" worth having.

points.what: "73% — 82.9 of 113.0 GB · part 3 of 4" sat under the model name, three lines above the bar it was describing.
points.fix: It now sits centred directly above the bar, so the number and the thing it measures are together.
points.why:
Under the name, the line was competing with the model's identity and the quality line. Above the bar it reads as a caption, which is what it is.

A row with no bar — a finished model, or a damaged one — has nothing to caption, so its size stays under the name exactly as before. Nothing moved on those two rows.

closing:
Verification on this build

  • All six local-model screens captured covered in all six themes, zero partials, first pass.
  • Workbench boot check 12/12 against a server confirmed live.
  • Types, lint and the invariant scan clean on the renderer.

What happens next

With this signed off, the design is final and the rest is machinery you will not see until it works: the record written beside each download so a crash can be recovered from, one honest list that never calls a half-finished model "installed", the disk-space check counting what is left rather than the whole download, and Resume actually resuming. I will come back when it runs against real files rather than fake ones.
